title: Streak-free glass cleaner
subtitle: A fast-evaporating spray for windows and mirrors
excerpt: A three-ingredient glass cleaner of white vinegar, isopropyl alcohol, and water. The alcohol speeds evaporation for a streak-free finish on mirrors, windows, and glass surfaces. Makes 250 ml.
sourceNotes: Isopropyl alcohol in cleaning: open-access chemical safety data for isopropyl alcohol (IPA 70%); general formulation references. Vinegar streak removal: comparative studies of household cleaning agents, open-access consumer chemistry literature.

recipe.batchNotes: Doubles to 500 ml in a larger bottle.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix and store in the spray bottle; stable for a year.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps one year in a sealed spray bottle. The isopropyl alcohol slowly evaporates if the bottle is frequently opened; refresh with a small top-up if the formula weakens. Discard if the liquid changes colour or smells sharp and unclean.

glossaryTerms.definition: A short-chain alcohol that evaporates quickly, taking surface residue with it. At 30% or higher in a cleaning spray, it prevents the water phase leaving smears as it dries.

content.text: This is a streak-free glass cleaner for mirrors, windows, and glass splashbacks. The
evaporates quickly, carrying the dissolved grime away before it can settle back as a smear. The vinegar cuts fingerprints and light grease.
Use in a ventilated room. Do not spray near an open flame. Avoid contact with skin; if it splashes, rinse with water.

items.prepNote: 99% IPA from a hardware store or chemist; dilutes to roughly 40% in the finished spray
distilled rather than tap to avoid the white residue that dissolved minerals leave on glass

content.text: Measure the isopropyl alcohol into the spray bottle.
Top up with the distilled water. Fit the spray cap and shake gently.

Spray lightly onto the glass surface. Wipe with a lint-free cloth or a crumpled sheet of newspaper in a circular motion, then buff with a dry cloth. Apply in the shade or on a cool day; the alcohol evaporates too fast in direct sunlight and can leave marks before it has cleaned.

Safe on plain glass, mirrors with silver backing, and glass-ceramic cooktops. Do not use on acrylic or plexiglass (the alcohol can cloud it), on anti-reflective coated glass (the acid may strip the coating), or on tinted windows.
Store in a sealed spray bottle in a cool cupboard away from heat sources. Keeps one year.
